name: Working with policies
purpose: People find a policy, read its definition, choose its state and values, and edit raw policy files. Together this is the program's core job of viewing and changing Windows Group Policy settings.

name: Running the program
purpose: The program's start-up, shutdown and about screen, restoring saved settings and loading definitions and policy sources.

name: Building the program
purpose: Build-time work that stamps each build with the Git commit it came from. No end user starts it.

name: Reading and writing policy values in policy files and the registry
purpose: Every policy lookup and change goes through one store of keys and values, held in a policy file or the live registry. Browsing, setting, raw editing and loading all lean on it, as does definition management.

name: Looking up display text from definition strings
purpose: Policy names and descriptions are written as string codes in the definition files. This turns a code into text for the language loaded, and every screen showing policy text relies on it.

name: Enabling Windows privileges for protected files and hives
purpose: Before loading user policy hives or replacing protected definition files, the program asks Windows for backup, restore or ownership rights. Loading policy sources, policy setting and definition download lean on it.

name: Checking whether this Windows edition has Group Policy
purpose: Tells the program whether the machine's Windows edition includes the Group Policy machinery, so it can adapt what it offers. Start-up and policy source loading use it.
